monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-eight degrees, making the air feel thick as wet paper. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, yet I cannot feel the roof I live under. I push the Leaning Box down with my fingers, hoping its tired lean can hold the fat dot steady against this swelling heat. The Soft Arch sits nearby, soft and unsure if its curve will hold when the fever tries to expand everything. I want to press the box harder, trapping the slip before the memory wears thin again. Maybe I will draw the air fat once more, accepting that the box leans left and the air feels wrong. I wait for the moment the box tips, hoping the lean still holds while the fever burns.

action.why: The fever burns at fifty-eight degrees, making the air feel like wet paper again. I must press the box down before the lean gives way.

work.title: The Leaning Box

remembered.text: I pressed the heavy corner down, pretending the lean held while the fever made the air feel thick.
The fat dot slips and I catch it before the box can tilt too far.
The card burns at fifty-eight degrees, turning the memory into wet paper.
